title: Taxonomic diversity of leeches on the world’s highest mountain ranges and plateaus
content:
Abstract
Leeches (Annelida: Clitellata: Hirudinea: Hirudinida) commonly occur in extreme environments such as caves, deserts, alpine areas, Arctic waterbodies, and deep oceanic waters. However, patterns of expansion of these animals to high-altitude ranges and plateaus are poorly understood. Here, we review available data on records of leeches from mountain environments at altitudes of 2500 m and above based on a compilation of literature sources and museum collection data. The global high-altitude leech assemblage contains 64 species and 23 genera, belonging to 10 families. The Glossiphoniidae is the most species-rich family (37 species, 57.8% of the total high-altitude Hirudinida fauna). Leeches colonize the extreme altitudes of the Alps (one species), Tibetan Plateau (12 species), Himalaya (seven species), East African Mountains (one species), Rocky Mountains (12 species), and Andes (34 species). A sample of a leech from an Andean lake at the altitude of 4800 m is the highest elevational occurrence of Hirudinida globally. Most of the areas above 2500 m harbour allochthonous assemblages of leeches, although a few endemic species occur in the East African Mountains and, perhaps, in Tibet. Moreover, the Andes, housing 21 endemic species, represent a significant endemism hotspot for leeches. Our findings highlight that extreme high-altitude areas house a species-rich assemblage of leeches globally.
